history.summary: Temblai Devi (Tryamboli) is a form of Renuka Devi, an incarnation of Durga, presiding over a hilltop temple in eastern Kolhapur; the hillock is named Temblai hill after the temple. The complex has two shrines: the larger southern one for Temblai Devi and a smaller northeastern one for Yamai Devi, plus a large open-air Ganpati idol, a bust of Chhatrapati Shivaji, and a children's park. Legend says Renuka is Mahalakshmi's sister and helped her slay the demons of the region, but after victory Mahalakshmi gave her no due respect - so Renuka sat on the hill with her back turned, which is why the Mahalaxmi idol faces west while Temblai Devi faces east. Women devotees especially pray here for marriage or their husband's wellbeing. In the pre-independence era the breezy hill was a centre for treating tuberculosis patients. A second, smaller Temblai shrine stands at Kadamwadi on the Panchganga river. Founding date and builder are not recorded in consulted sources.

town_description: Kolhapur is a major city in southwest Maharashtra on the Panchganga river, former capital of the Kolhapur Maratha state and now district headquarters. It is one of Maharashtra's leading pilgrimage centres (Mahalakshmi, Jyotiba, Temblai) and famous for kushti wrestling, Kolhapuri chappals and its historic Bhavani Mandap complex.
